label: GPT-6 Luna
output:
**To whoever is putting rubbish in my bin,**

I’m writing this because I’m fed up with finding other people’s rubbish in my bin. It’s the grey Greenmount Bins one outside **No. 14, Aughrim Terrace**, with **14 painted in white on the lid**. It goes out on Tuesday night and is collected on Wednesday morning.

I got home at 3am last Tuesday after work and found the lid wouldn’t close. There were three full black bags in it, including one with nappies. They weren’t mine. This has been happening for about a month now, and it’s not just a few bits left behind — it’s full bags.

Greenmount charges by weight: **41 cent per kilo**. My last bill was **€63.20 for two months**, when it’s usually around €25. I’m not paying extra for someone else’s rubbish. I rent the place, and I’m not prepared to keep covering the cost of bags I didn’t put in the bin.

If you’re stuck and need to get rid of something, ask. I can tell you who to ring; it’s not hard to sort out properly. But putting full bags in my bin without asking has to stop. Whoever’s doing it: please leave my bin alone from now on.

I found a gas-bill envelope in one of the bags, but the name had been torn off and it only had the terrace on it. I’m not looking to make a big scene or start pointing fingers, but I do want to be clear that I’ve noticed what’s happening. Someone across the road also saw a car pull up on Tuesday evening, though they didn’t see who it was.

I work nights, so I’m often getting home when the rest of the road is asleep. That doesn’t mean I won’t notice, and it doesn’t mean I’ll keep letting this happen. If the bags keep appearing, I’ll start locking the bin with a padlock.

Please respect my bin and stop putting your rubbish in it. I’m not a pushover, and I’m not paying for this anymore.

**The person at No. 14**
